FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the dratl finalized by the Plastics Sectional Committee had been approved by the Petroleum, Coal and Related Products Division Council. Tetrabromobisphenol-A is used for flame retardant applications in polymeric resin such as thermoplastics, thermosetting, rubber foams, coatings, etc and other products like textiles, etc. For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2:1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)'. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

ANNEX A [Table 1, S1 No. (i)]
DETERMINATION A-1 APPARATUS A-1.l High Performance (Isocratic) A-1.2 UV-VIS Detector A-1.3 Data Station A-1.4 Printer A-1.5 Micro Litre Syringe A-1.6 Volumetric Flask, 100 ml. A-1.7 Column, C18 micro Bondapak. A-2 REAGENTS A-2.1 Methanol A-2.2 Water A-2.3 Acetic Acid A-3 SAMPLE PREPARATION A-3. 1 Weigh accurately about 0.100 g of sample in 100 ml volumetric flask and dissolve in methanol and make up to volume with methanol. Filter through Whatman filter paper No. 42. 2 Liquid Chromatograph OF ASSAY BY CHROMATOGRAPHIC A-3.2 Mobile Phase Mobile phase is 80 (methanol): 20 (15 percent acetic acid in water). Flow rate: 1.0 mllmin. A-3.3 Run Time 10.0 min. A-4 PROCEDURE Switch on the mains and start the instrument. Prime the pump for about 5.0 min and flush the system with 100 percent methanol for half an hour, then flush the system with the mobile phase for half an hour. Set the detector at 290 nm. Check the base line, if a steady base line is observed then inject 20 VI standard tetrabromobisphenol-A and run the instrument for 10 min. Note down the retention time. Then inject 20 pl test sample and note down the retention time. A sharp peak appears at about 6.8 min is tetrabromobisphenol-A. (An impurity peak, tribromobisphenol-A peak appears at about 5.4 rein, bisphenol-A peak appears at about 3.7 rein). Note down the area percent of each peak from the chromatogram and report (100 percentage of corqponents other than tetrabromobisphenol-A is the chromatographic purity of TBBA). ANALYSIS

DETERMINATION B-1 APPARATUS B-1.l Glass Heating Vessel --Suitable construction and capacity containing one of the following or another suitable liquid, to a height of not less than 14 cm. B-1. 1.1 Liquid Paraffin boiling point
-- Having sufficiently high

B

[Table 1, S1 No. (ii)]
OF MELTING POINT B-2 PROCEDURE B-2.1 Dry a small quantity of the finely powdered substance at 105 + 2�C for 2 h. Transfer a portion to a dry capillary tube and pack the powder by tapping on a hard surface so as to form a tightly packed column 4 to 6 mm in height. Heat a suitable liquid in the heating vessel and regulate the rate of rise of temperature prior to the introduction of the capillary tube to 1�/min, when the temperature reaches 10� below the lowest figure of the range for the substance being tested insert the capillary tube. The temperature at which the last particle disappear is regarded as the melting point of the substance, for substances that decomposes the temperature at which frothing begins. Correct the observed temperature for any error in the calibration of the thermometer and of the difference, if any. B-2.2 The apparatus should be periodically calibrated using certified reference substances of declared melting point.

B-1.1.2 Silicone Fluid -- Having sufficiently high boiling point. B-1.2 Suitable Stirring Device -- Capable of rapidly mixing the liquid. B-1.3 Calibrated Thermometer -- Suitable for the substance being carried complying with the requirements. B-1.4 Thin Walled Capillary, of hard glass, closed at one end, with a wall thickness of 0.10 to 0.15 mm at least 12 cm in length and of internal diameter 0.9 to 1.1 mm. The tubes should be preferably be kept sealed at both ends and cuts as required.

ANNEX C [Table 1, Sl No. (iii)]
DETERMINATION C-1 APPARATUS OF COLOUR (APHA) C-2.2 Methanol C-3 PROCEDURE Prepare standards of 10, 20 and 30 Hazen units in methanol using the 500 Hazen unit stock solution. Prepare a 20 percent sample solution in methanol by dissolving 4.0 g sample in 20 ml of methanol. Filter the solution through Whatman filter paper No. 42. Set the UV-VIS spectropkotometer at 385 nm, use methanol as blank, make auto zero, using methanol. Put the standard 10 hazen unit standard solution and make auto concentration 10.0 and check the concentration for 20 and 30 hazen standard solutions. Now put the sample solution, record the concentration and report the colour as APHA.

C-1.1 Spectrophotometer C-1.2 Cuvettes, 1 cm. C-2 REAGENTS

C-2.1 Standard 500 Hazen Unit Solution Prepare 500 Hazen unit standard solution by dissolving 0.25 g of cobalt chloride and 0.2625 g of chloroplatinic acid (or 0.311 3 g of potassium chloroplatinate) with 25 ml of concentrated hydrochloric acid in a 250 ml volumetric flask and dilute it up to the mark with demineralized water.

H

[Table 1, S1 No. (viii)]
OF IRON CONTENT hydrochloride in 60 ml water, filter and make up to 100 ml with water. H-2.4 1,10 Phenanthroline Solution--Dissolve 0.9 g 1,10 phenanthroline monohydrate in 30 ml of methanol and dilute to 300 ml with water. H-2.5 Ammonium Acetate-Acetic Acid Solution -- Dissolve 200 g of ammonium acetate in 600 ml water, filter and add 50 ml of acetic acid and dilute to 1000 ml with water. H-2.6 Standard Iron Solution -- Dissolve 7.02168 g of ferrous ammonium sulphate (100 percent) in 100 ml water and add 30 ml of concentrated. sulphuric acid and make up to 1 000 ml in a volumetric flask (1 000 ppm). 1 ml of this solution contains 1.0 mg. Take 5.0 ml and dilute to 500 ml in a volumetric flask (10 ppm) .1 ml of this solution is equivalent to 10 microgram of iron. 5

H-2.2 Water -- HPLC grade. H-2.3 10 Percent Hydroxylamine Hydrochloride Solution -- Dissolve 10 g A.R. grade hydroxylamine

IS 15621:2005 H-3 PROCEDURE Take 20 to 25 g of sample, add 20 ml concentrated hydrochloric acid and 20 ml water in a 150 ml round bottom flask fitted with a reflux condenser. Boil this mixture for 20 min. Cool the mixture to room temperature. Filter this solution through a Whatman fiber paper No. 42 and dilute to 100 ml in a volumetric flask. Take 25 ml of this clear filtrate solution in a clean 100 ml beaker. Add 5.0 ml of 10 percent hydroxylamine hydrochloride, 5 ml 1,10 phenanthroline reagent and adjust the pH to 3.5 using pH meter and acetic acid ammonium acetate solution (25 ml required). Add 5.0 ml more of this buffer and dilute up to 100 ml in a volumetric flask with distilled water. For blank solution, take 20 ml A.R grade hydrochloric acid and dilute to 100.0 ml with distilled water. Take 25 ml of this solution and add same quantity of reagents and adjust the pH to 3.5 using acetic acid-ammonium acetate buffer and dilute to 100 ml in a volumetric flask. For standard solution, pipette out 5 microgram (0.5 ml), 10 microgram (1.0 ml) and 20 microgram (2.0 ml) of standard iron solution in three different 100 ml volumetric flask and add 25 ml of blank, same quantity of reagents and adjust the pH to 3.5 using ammonium acetate - acetic acid solution. Allow to stand all the prepared solutions for 15 min. Set the UV-VIS spectrophotometer at 510 nm. Make auto concentration zero using blank solution. Put 10 pg standard iron solution and make the concentration 10.0, and check the concentration for 5.0 ~g iron and 20.0 pg iron standard solution. Now take the reading for sample, let this be Y. Calculate the iron content in the sample as follows. H-4 CALCULATION y x 4.0 Iron content, ppm where M= mass of sample, in g; and Y= reading of sample. = M

DETERMINATION J-1 APPARATUS J-1.l Karl Fischer Titrator J-2 REAGENTS J-2.1 KF Reagent J-2.2 Methanol -- A.R. grade (~ee IS 517). J-2.3 Distilled Water J-3 PROCEDURE J-3. 1 Add about 20 ml of methanol to the titration J-3.2 Take 2 g sample in case of moisture content less than 1 percent and 1 g sample in case of moisture content 1 to 5 percent and 0.5 g sample in the case of moisture content between 5 to 10 percent. OF MOISTURE CONTENT vessel and titrate it with Karl Fischer reagent, once the titration is over calibrate the instrument with 10 ml water and enter the value, and the factor will be stored in the memory automatically. Add known quantity of the test sample in to the reaction vessel and start titration. When the end point is reached enter the weight of sample and instrument will automatically calculate and displays the moisture content of the sample in ppm.

L-2 REAGENTS L-2. 1 Concentrated Nitric Acid, see IS 264.

L-2.2 Eschka Mixture -- Thoroughly mix 2 parts by weight of light calcined magnesium oxide with 1 part of anhydrous sodium carbonate. L-2.3 Silver Nitrate, 0.5 N. L-2.4 Ammonium Thiocyanate, 0.1 N. L-3 PROCEDURE L-3.1 Weigh 0.2-0.3 g of sample in a nickel or platinum crucible containing 2 g of Eschka mixture in it. Slowly fuse the mixture for 2 h under low flame to avoid escape of bromine vapors and then cool to room temperature. Dissolve the material completely

with minimum quantity of concentrated nitric acid, till it is acidic. Digest the mixture for 15 min and dilute with water to 250 ml in a volumetric flask. Take 25 ml of the solution to a 150 ml conical flask, add lml cone. nitric acid, 20 ml of 0.1 N AgNOt solution, 3-4 drops of nitrobenzene and 10-15 drops of ferroin indicator. Titrate against 0.1 N ammonium thiocyanate solution till pale brick red end point is obtained. Note the volume of thiocyanate consumed (A). Carry out the blank titration witbout sample. Note the volume of thiocyanate consumed (B). Calculate the bromine content and report. L-4 CALCULATION
(B -A) x N x 79.904 M

ANNEX M (Clause 6)
SAMPLING M-1 LOT OF TETRABROMOBISPHENOL-A

to constitute the required sample size. M-2.2 From each bag selected according to M-2.1.1 take approximately equal quantity of material fkom different positions of the bag so as to form a composite sample weighing about 250 g which shall be divided into three test samples, one each for buyer, seller and reference. Each test sample shall be transferred to a glass sample container and sealed air-tight. Label the containers with date of sampling and other particulars of the material and the lot.
M-3 NUMBER OF TESTS The tests for all the requirements shall be carried out

All the bags of the material in a single consignment belonging to the same batch of manufacture shall be grouped together to constitute a lot. M-2 SCALE OF SAMPLING M-2. 1 Each lot shall be sampled separately. The number of bags to be selected from a lot shall depend on the size of the lot and shall be in accordance with Table 2. M-2. 1.1 These bags shall be selected at random from the lot. In order to ensure the randomness of selection, procedures given in IS 4905 may be referred to. In the absence of random number tables, the following procedure may be followed: Starting from any bag in the lot, count them as 1,2,3, . . .. upto r and so on in one order, where r is the integral part of N/n, N being the lot size and n the sample size. Every rth bag thus counted shall be withdrawn from the lot so as

on the composite sample as obtained in M-2.2. M-4 CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY The lot shall be considered to be in conformity with the requirements of this specification, if all the test results on the composite sample obtained in M-3 satisfi the corresponding requirements as specified in this standard.

Table 2 Number of Bags to be Selected from the Lot (Clause M-2. 1)
Number of Bags in the Lot N (1) up to 5 6-50 51-100 101-300 301-500 501-1000 1001 and above Number of Bags to be Selected n (2) MI 5 8 13 20 32 50

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision.
